timeline_events.summary: Airey Neave, shadow secretary of state for Northern Ireland and a close friend of Margaret Thatcher, died when a car bomb exploded at the House of Commons car park.
Margaret Thatcher led the Conservative Party to victory over Jim Callaghan's Labour Party in the UK general election, becoming prime minister with a 43-seat majority.
Margaret Thatcher left Downing Street for the last time and officially informed the Queen of her resignation.

John Major wrote a five-page personal letter to Margaret Thatcher to inform her of his government's decision to abolish her flagship poll tax, which he described as unfair, uncollectable and indefensible.
A new Russian political party, the Conservative Party - Thatcherites of Russia, plans to launch later in the month in St Petersburg, basing itself on Thatcherism and Margaret Thatcher.

Six years after the poll tax's abolition, an estimated 4,000,000 non-payers of up to £5 billion in community charge became immune from prosecution under a six-year statute of limitation, meaning outstanding money will never be recovered.
John Major's memoirs reveal he secretly drew up plans to stand for the Tory leadership while publicly supporting Margaret Thatcher during the 1990 leadership contest that led to her downfall.
Sir William van Straubenzee, a former Tory MP and One Nation wet who led backbench opponents of Margaret Thatcher after she became party leader in 1975, died aged 75.

Tony Blair, who privately describes Margaret Thatcher as a "great" leader, appears to have taken a leaf out of the former prime minister's book by embracing new Russian president Vladimir Putin with such eagerness.
Brighton bomber Patrick Magee claimed his 1984 attack on the Grand Hotel, which nearly killed Margaret Thatcher, forced the British government to open negotiations with the IRA.
William Hague's early support for the Liberal party before Margaret Thatcher deposed Ted Heath and he crossed over to the Tories is uncovered by his biographer.
Margaret Thatcher is described as having worked like a coal heaver and sleeping only four hours a night, which saved her from harm in the 1984 Brighton bombing.

Margaret Thatcher's first recorded intervention in Edward Heath's cabinet was to propose imposing borrowing charges on library books and abolishing free school milk for children over seven, though the library charge idea was later dropped.
Margaret Thatcher publicly declared she would never support the pound joining the euro, undermining William Hague's Conservative Party campaign policy on Europe.
John Campbell's book "Margaret Thatcher: The Grocer's Daughter" is listed among his top 10 political biographies.
Sir Denis Thatcher opens a new building at Cambridge University's Churchill College Archives Centre to house Margaret Thatcher's papers.
The article mentions that Margaret Thatcher, 22 years earlier, resolved in a secret meeting with her chancellor to double VAT shortly after the Conservative Party won an election.
Margaret Thatcher backs Iain Duncan Smith in the Tory leadership contest, warning that rival Kenneth Clarke would lead the party to disaster.
Margaret Thatcher says Muslims have not done enough to condemn the terrorist attacks on America.
A revival of Caryl Churchill's 1982 play Top Girls, which was inspired by Margaret Thatcher's election and right-wing feminism, is acclaimed in London as a modern classic.
ITV1 announces a three-part documentary about Margaret Thatcher's rise to become the UK's first woman prime minister, to be delivered in December.
Margaret Thatcher decides to bow out of public life, ending her career as a retired prime minister.
Conservative Party leader Iain Duncan Smith pledges to change the party's "uncaring" image and move past Margaret Thatcher's legacy, following her retirement from public life on medical grounds.
An adviser to Margaret Thatcher says she would have lost the Falklands war in 1982 if America had failed to provide crucial Sidewinder missiles to bolster British air defences.

Margaret Thatcher's former foreign secretary Geoffrey Howe delivered a resignation speech to the House of Commons comparing being one of her cabinet ministers to having his bat broken by the team captain.

Sir William Shelton, who was Margaret Thatcher's unofficial "chief whip" in her 1975 Conservative leadership campaign and later one of her parliamentary private secretaries, died at 73 from Alzheimer's disease.
Article cites Margaret Thatcher’s 1982 announcement of the Franks inquiry into the Falklands as a model for a proposed inquiry into the Iraq war.
Sir Denis Thatcher, husband of Margaret Thatcher, died at the age of 88.

Sir Denis Thatcher, in a posthumously aired TV interview, criticized John Major as a "ghastly prime minister" and blamed the 1990 "treachery" against Margaret Thatcher for subsequent Conservative defeats.

Margaret Thatcher's papers up to the time she became prime minister were opened to the public at Churchill College, Cambridge, and released online, generating so much interest that it threatened to overwhelm her website.
A biography of Margaret Thatcher by John Campbell is reviewed, discussing her premiership and its impact on Britain.
A profile notes Margaret Thatcher was born 79 years ago in Grantham and served as Britain's first female prime minister.
Margaret Thatcher celebrated the 25th anniversary of her election victory at a tribute dinner in London.
Conservative central office, the party headquarters associated with Margaret Thatcher's election victories, closes as staff move to a new building.
Margaret Thatcher was awake working on her Conservative party conference speech when the IRA bomb destroyed the Grand Hotel in Brighton in autumn 1984.

Patrick Magee, the IRA terrorist who bombed the 1984 Conservative Party conference in an attempt to kill Margaret Thatcher and her Cabinet, stated he would plant the bomb again and claimed the attack aided the Irish peace process.
A timeline notes that Margaret Thatcher became prime minister in May 1979 and was ousted as Conservative leader and prime minister in November 1990.
Patrick Magee, the IRA bomber who planted the 1984 Brighton hotel bomb targeting Margaret Thatcher and her cabinet, returns to Brighton for the first time since the attack on its 20th anniversary.

An edited excerpt from Norman Tebbit's essay in the book "Margaret Thatcher's Revolution" discusses Margaret Thatcher's political career, her promotion of certain men who later defeated her, and the resulting divisions in the Conservative party.
Article notes the 25th anniversary of Margaret Thatcher's accession as Prime Minister, while reflecting on Jim Callaghan's loss to her in the 1979 election.
Article recounts Margaret Thatcher’s 1979 election campaign and her subsequent rise to become the UK’s first woman prime minister.
A copy of a national newspaper signed by Margaret Thatcher the day after she quit as prime minister sold at auction for £270.
The British arm of the Margaret Thatcher Foundation, established by Margaret Thatcher in 1991, was formally dissolved at Companies House two days before the general election amid declining finances.
Margaret Thatcher is mentioned in an obituary of Edward Heath as having won the Conservative leadership from Heath in 1975 and as having a mutually disliked relationship with him.
Queen Elizabeth II is to attend Margaret Thatcher's 80th birthday celebration at the Mandarin Oriental Hotel in Knightsbridge.
Margaret Thatcher turned 80.
Article recalls Margaret Thatcher's 1975 Conservative leadership victory, when a stalking-horse strategy unexpectedly led to her winning the first ballot against Edward Heath.
Article recalls that Margaret Thatcher informed Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev of the 1988 Armenian earthquake via telegram.
A musical based on the life of Margaret Thatcher, "Thatcher: The Musical," is set to have its UK premiere at the Warwick Arts Centre.
Foursight Theatre's musical production about Margaret Thatcher premiered at the Warwick Arts Centre.
Shadow chancellor George Osborne invokes Margaret Thatcher to defend the Conservative leadership's decision not to promise early tax cuts.
Former editors Charles Moore and Simon Jenkins debate Margaret Thatcher's legacy at a Policy Exchange fringe event during the Conservative Party conference.
Lord Peyton of Yeovil, who unsuccessfully stood against Margaret Thatcher for the Tory leadership in 1975 and was excluded from her cabinet in 1979, died aged 87.
Norman Miscampbell, a progressive Conservative MP who was rejected as a rebellious "wet" by Margaret Thatcher and privately warned her against the poll tax, died aged 81.
A film about Margaret Thatcher, titled Maggie the Movie, is being written by Brian Fillis, focusing on the period leading up to the Falklands War.
Tony Blair says he would have fought the Falklands war in Margaret Thatcher's position because it was "the right thing to do."
Lord Carrington, who served as foreign secretary under Margaret Thatcher from 1979 until his April 1982 resignation over the Falklands invasion, is the subject of an article.
John Biffen, former Conservative cabinet minister during Margaret Thatcher's era, died in hospital aged 76.
The BBC removed a scene from a drama about Margaret Thatcher in which she was depicted swearing, after complaints that she did not use bad language.
A new play by Tom Green speculates on the legacy and supposed death of former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher.
Former British foreign secretary Francis Pym, who served under Margaret Thatcher during the Falklands War and was later sacked by her, died at age 86 after a prolonged illness.
BBC4 broadcasts the drama Margaret Thatcher: The Long Walk to Finchley, starring Andrea Riseborough as a young Margaret Thatcher.

Former cabinet minister Norman Fowler recounts that his 1990 resignation from Margaret Thatcher's cabinet was motivated by a desire to spend more time with his young family, a decision he says was accepted by fellow MPs including John Major.
A state funeral is planned for Margaret Thatcher.
Margaret Thatcher is to return to Chequers at the invitation of Gordon Brown for a low-key lunch to discuss the global downturn.

Article compares Gordon Brown's political situation to Margaret Thatcher's 1989/1990 leadership challenges, noting Thatcher was forced out of Downing Street within six weeks of being cheered at the 1990 Conservative party conference.
Conservative conference delegates at a Guardian fringe meeting vote Margaret Thatcher the greatest Tory hero of all time.
An exhibition preview discusses a group show curated by Olivia Plender that questions the results of Margaret Thatcher's 1978 "There is no alternative" call to individualism.
Daily Mail sketchwriter Quentin Letts publishes a book extract arguing that Margaret Thatcher's response to the miners' strike did lasting damage to Britain.
The airwaves featured Margaret Thatcher in a documentary and a BBC2 dramatisation of her 1990 ousting, amid anniversaries of her 1979 election and the 1984-5 miners' strike.
The BBC drama "Margaret" was broadcast, portraying Margaret Thatcher's final days as prime minister, with an earlier draft containing scenes more critical of her that were cut from the final version.
The article notes that it is almost 19 years since Margaret Thatcher’s leadership tottered when her new local poll tax triggered riots and looting in London.
Margaret Thatcher appeared at Chelsea Hospital with Prince Charles to open an infirmary named in her honor.
The BBC broadcasts its 1979 election special to mark the 30th anniversary of Margaret Thatcher's arrival in Downing Street.
The article discusses the ruined reputation of Margaret Thatcher on the anniversary of her 1979 election, amid debate over her legacy following the financial crisis.

Nicholas Boles, an adviser to David Cameron, said he hoped the Conservatives would not win by a landslide, recalling Francis Pym's 1983 admission that prompted Margaret Thatcher to sack him as foreign secretary.
Margaret Thatcher returned to Downing Street.

Cabinet papers from Margaret Thatcher's earliest days as prime minister are released under the 30-year rule, revealing her pugnacious style through hostile handwritten marginal notes on government documents.
Labour leadership candidate John McDonnell joked at a GMB union hustings event that he wanted to go back in time to the 1980s to "assassinate Thatcher."
Newly released 1980 papers show Margaret Thatcher’s private secretary Ian Gow, with her permission, encouraged rightwing MPs’ opposition to employment secretary Jim Prior’s trade union bill.
Meryl Streep won the best actress award from the New York Critics Circle for her performance as Margaret Thatcher in the biopic The Iron Lady.

Secret Thatcher files reveal Rupert Murdoch met Margaret Thatcher at Chequers on 4 January 1981 before his Times takeover bid, contradicting the official Times history's account that they had no communication during the bid period.
A senior Tory criticizes David Cameron by saying he is no Margaret Thatcher and is instead the party's new Ted Heath.

Newly released government papers reveal Margaret Thatcher was willing to be flexible during the 1982 Falklands conflict and that she and her chancellor considered proposals that would have ended the National Health Service.
Margaret Thatcher's coffin was placed in the chapel of St Mary Undercroft before her funeral.
Margaret Thatcher's death was announced by her children Mark and Carol Thatcher in a statement expressing their great sadness.
Publishers announce that an authorised biography of Margaret Thatcher and a tribute by her speechwriter Robin Harris will be released later in April, following her death from a stroke.

Margaret Thatcher's death prompted sharply divided reactions in Argentina and the Falkland Islands, with islanders mourning her for sending a taskforce to liberate the islands in 1982 while Argentinians largely condemned her.

The article discusses Margaret Thatcher's political heirs and allies, noting that most Tory MPs regarded themselves as supporters of Lady Thatcher, but only a handful knew her well after her retirement from public life in 2002.
Margaret Thatcher's death is announced at the age of 87.
Several hundred people gathered in Brixton and Glasgow to celebrate Margaret Thatcher's death with street parties.
A Guardian/ICM poll conducted on the afternoon of Margaret Thatcher's death finds public opinion divided on her legacy, with 50% rating her premiership as good for Britain and 34% as bad.

After Margaret Thatcher's death was announced, the producers of Billy Elliot: the Musical asked audience members to vote on whether a song calling for her death should be performed, and it was performed after a near-unanimous verdict.

Commentators reflect on Margaret Thatcher's legacy in theatre and the arts following her death, focusing on her shift from public subsidy to corporate sponsorship and the lasting effect of her values on British culture.
A Guardian/ICM poll released on the afternoon of Margaret Thatcher's death shows mixed public support for her flagship policies, with 50% rating her 11-year premiership as good for Britain.
Martin McGuinness calls for an end to republicans celebrating Margaret Thatcher's death, while further celebrations are planned for her funeral next week.
A Democratic Unionist assembly member condemns republican celebrations in Derry and Belfast following the death of Margaret Thatcher.
Calls gather momentum for a statue of Margaret Thatcher to be erected in Trafalgar Square, with Defence Secretary Philip Hammond and others suggesting a memorial in London.
Australian foreign minister Bob Carr claims Margaret Thatcher held "unabashedly racist" views, revealing she warned him against Asian immigration in Australia.

Parliament was recalled for a seven-and-a-half-hour session of Commons tributes to Margaret Thatcher, led by David Cameron and Ed Miliband, after Downing Street departed from a long-agreed plan and past precedent.
Metropolitan police Sergeant Jeremy Scott resigned after allegedly tweeting that he hoped Margaret Thatcher's death was "painful and degrading."
A dress rehearsal takes place in central London for the military procession of Margaret Thatcher's ceremonial funeral.

Margaret Thatcher's death certificate was made public, recording her occupation as "retired stateswoman" and her cause of death as a cardiovascular accident, while her coffin was brought to the Chapel of St Mary Undercroft ahead of her funeral.
The ceremonial funeral of former UK Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher was held at St Paul's Cathedral, attended by Queen Elizabeth II and dignitaries from 170 countries.
David Dimbleby is to anchor the BBC's coverage of Margaret Thatcher's ceremonial funeral at St Paul's Cathedral in London.
Police are planning a large-scale security operation for Margaret Thatcher's ceremonial funeral in central London, assessing potential threats from protesters and dissident terrorists.

The bishop of London claimed in his funeral address that Margaret Thatcher was part of the team that invented Mr Whippy ice-cream, a claim disputed by reports noting there is no firm evidence she directly assisted in the invention of soft ice-cream.
Following Margaret Thatcher's death, an article examines her housing policies' legacy and role in the UK's housing crisis.
The first volume of Charles Moore's authorised biography of Margaret Thatcher, Not For Turning, is published immediately after her funeral.
Margaret Thatcher's grandchildren Michael and Amanda are to lead her funeral procession, with Amanda reading a lesson at the funeral.
Margaret Thatcher's funeral featured a Falklands theme, with military personnel from units that served in the 1982 conflict participating in the ceremony.

The first volume of Charles Moore's authorised biography of Margaret Thatcher is published, revealing a memo from adviser Sir John Hoskyns warning her within two years of becoming prime minister that she was bullying weaker colleagues and abusing her seniority.
Charles Moore's authorized biography of Margaret Thatcher outsold Robin Harris's biography in first-week sales.

Newly released 1984 cabinet papers reveal Margaret Thatcher secretly prepared to use troops and declare a state of emergency during the miners' strike over fears Britain would run out of food and grind to a halt.
Charles Moore's authorised biography of Margaret Thatcher is shortlisted for the Orwell prize.

Newly released Downing Street files from 1985 and 1986 reveal that cabinet critics warned Margaret Thatcher about the fiscal and political impact of the poll tax, but their objections were brushed aside.
Margaret Thatcher's family donated a tranche of her personal papers to the Churchill Archives Centre in return for £1m off their inheritance tax bill.
Geoffrey Howe, whose 1990 resignation speech was widely seen as the central factor in forcing Margaret Thatcher from Downing Street, dies aged 88.
More than 150 items from Margaret Thatcher's estate, including her dispatch box, wedding dress, power suits, and handbags, are being sold at auction at Christie's in London.

Newly released National Archives documents reveal that Margaret Thatcher was allegedly given an undeclared diamond and emerald necklace by a Middle Eastern oil minister in 1982, prompting concern inside No 10.
Denis Thatcher wrote a letter to BBC board of governors chairman Marmaduke Hussey condemning a satirical Radio 4 story about Margaret Thatcher legalising hard drugs as "disgraceful and libellous."
Former Conservative cabinet minister Cecil Parkinson, a close ally of Margaret Thatcher, died of cancer aged 84.

The government's Social Mobility Commission published a report finding that the generation which grew up under Margaret Thatcher was the first since World War II to start with lower incomes than their parents.
Lord Prior, a cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher who was regarded as a leading "wet" dissenting from her radical politics, died aged 89.
Margaret Thatcher was added to the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography with a 30,000-word biography, the third longest entry in the work.
A book review discusses John Campbell's biography "Margaret Thatcher Volume One: The Grocer's Daughter," which examines Margaret Thatcher's early life and rise to power.
Margaret Thatcher studied chemistry at Oxford and worked as a research chemist, helping devise the process that produces Mr Whippy ice cream.
No topic-related event involving Margaret Thatcher is reported; the article only mentions her past work as a chemist before entering politics.
Sir Denis Thatcher, husband of Margaret Thatcher, died at age 88.
Margaret Thatcher's death was featured on newspaper front pages.
Margaret Thatcher hailed Mikhail Gorbachev as a man she could do business with, helping open the Soviet Union to the West and unfreeze the Cold War.
Article criticizes Margaret Thatcher's economic policies and legacy, arguing she was not popular and did not deliver economic success.
Margaret Thatcher is portrayed in multiple television dramatisations, including upcoming BBC2 reconstruction Coup!, with no single main event.
Margaret Thatcher is not the subject of a current event; the article discusses her legacy and inspiration to Conservative campaigners in Finchley and Golders Green ahead of the 2010 election.
Article discusses Margaret Thatcher's background as a scientist and how it may have influenced her political ideology, but reports no specific event.
Margaret Thatcher's funeral was covered on newspaper front pages.

facts.text: On 1979-05-03 Margaret Thatcher led the Conservative Party to victory over Jim Callaghan's Labour Party in the UK general election, becoming prime minister with a 43-seat majority.
On 1990-11-28 Margaret Thatcher left Downing Street for the last time and officially informed the Queen of her resignation.
On 2003-06-26 Sir Denis Thatcher, husband of Margaret Thatcher, died at the age of 88.
On 2013-04-08 Margaret Thatcher's death was announced at age 87 by her children Mark and Carol, prompting sharply divided reactions in Argentina and the Falkland Islands.
On 2013-04-17 Margaret Thatcher's ceremonial funeral was held at St Paul's Cathedral, attended by Queen Elizabeth II and dignitaries from 170 countries.
On 2017-01-12 Margaret Thatcher was added to the Oxford Dictionary of National Biography with a 30,000-word biography, the third longest entry in the work.
On 2006-02-08 Foursight Theatre's musical production about Margaret Thatcher premiered at the Warwick Arts Centre.

On 2009-02-26 the BBC drama "Margaret" was broadcast, portraying Margaret Thatcher's final days as prime minister, with an earlier draft containing scenes more critical of her that were cut from the final version.
